correctness.rationale: Let f and g be the zero and one maps and r=n−1−j. The final states are f^(r+d)g(f^i(q)) and f^r g(f^(i+d)(q)). A zero-cycle of length p(d) with marker reset separates; a chain through the earlier marker position with two fixed terminals uses i+3 states; a suffix-counting saturated chain after a reset uses r+2. Conversely, a k below all three terms has L_k|d, i≥k−2 and r≥k−1. If the start's zero-orbit has entered any cycle after i steps, both marker positions coincide as states, and f^r=f^(r+d) everywhere. Otherwise its transient has exactly k−1 states, consuming the whole state space except for a single fixed point. Then both final zero maps are constant. This also excludes a one-state separator. For fixed d, balancing the prefix and suffix budgets yields floor((n−d+4)/2), including the endpoint n−d=1. To require at least k≥3 states the smallest eligible gap is L_(k−1), with n−d≥2k−4; the listed thresholds follow. Inverting the increasing thresholds using log L_m∼m proves the natural-log asymptotic. The frozen checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed. Their recorded exhaustive small-budget checks are finite only; the argument handles all n.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For k≥2, Fact 3 gives necessity of i≥k−2 and r≥k−1. Resetting the marker on an m-cycle for each 2≤m≤k gives necessity of L_k|d. Conversely if those conditions hold, write d=hL_k. Identity (1) with a left context removes h copies of L_k from the suffix of the first word, giving X^iY X^r. Apply Proposition 4 with outer contexts X^(i−k+2) (and additional copies of X^L_k at successive steps) and X^(r−k+1) to insert h copies of L_k in the prefix, reaching the second word. Thus sep>k holds exactly under the three stated conditions. Taking the first budget for which a condition fails is precisely the frozen minimum; minimizing the witness length gives the stated thresholds immediately. Crucially the older paper already proves the nonuniform identity with the same exceptional single-chain case.
